Sh. Sarabjeet Singh. vs Walia Electronics. & Ors. on 24 March, 2017
H. P. STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL
 COMMISSION SHIMLA
 First Appeal No. : 247/2016
 Date of Presentation: 22.07.2016
 Order Reserved On : 14.03.2017
 Date of Order : 24.03.2017
 ......
Sarabjeet Singh son of Shri Didar Singh resident of 128 Krishna
Nagar Shimla-171 001 H.P.
 ...... Appellant/Complainant.
 Versus

1. Walia Electronics Shimla First Floor 77 Lower Bazar
 Shimla through Sameer Walia.

 ....Respondent/opposite party No.1

2. Redington Services HTP Computers Chuahan Niwas Ground
 Flooor Khalini Shimla H.P through its Manager.
 ....Respondent/opposite party No.2

3. Redington India Ltd. 95 Mount Road Guindy Chennai 600 032
 through its Manager.
 ....Respondent/opposite party No.3

Coram
Hon'ble Justice P.S. Rana (R) President
Hon'ble Mr. Vijay Pal Khachi Member
Hon'ble Ms. Meena Verma Member

Whether approved for reporting?1 Yes.

For Appellant : Mr. Dheeraj Bansal Advocate.
For Respo ndents : Mr. Swaran Sharma Advocate.

JUSTICE P.S. RANA (R) PRESIDENT:

O R D E R :
- Present appeal is filed under
section 15
of

Consumer Protection Act 1986 against order passed by

Learned District Forum Shimla in consumer complaint

No.288/2012 title Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics &

Ors. decided on 08.06.2016.
1
Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the order? Yes.
 Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)

Brief facts of Case:
2. Complainant namely Sarabjeet Singh filed

complaint before learned District Forum pleaded therein that

complainant purchased Black Berry Curve 8520 mobile in

consideration amount of Rs.9700/- (Nine thousand seven

hundred) from the opposite party No.1 vide invoice Annexure-
C1. It is further pleaded that mobile due to some internal

snag was unable to read the memory card. It is further

pleaded that matter was reported to opposite party. It is

further pleaded that warranty period of 18 months was given

by the opposite party No.1 at the time of purchase. It is

further pleaded that opposite party No.1 asked the

complainant that he should seek the service of opposite party

No.2. It is further pleaded that complainant was assured by

opposite party No.2 that best service would be provided to

complainant. It is pleaded that handset was given to opposite

party No.2 and opposite party No.2 assured that problem

would be solved. It is further pleaded that after some time

complainant approached opposite party No.2 to get his

handset back but to his utter surprise opposite party No.2

told that handset could not be repaired. It is further pleaded

that opposite party No.2 also created scratches in handset. It

is further pleaded that thereafter complainant purchased a

new handset for his day to day working. Complainant sought

following reliefs (i) Replacement of Black Berry 8520 handset
2
Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)

purchased by complainant. (ii) In addition relief of litigation

costs to the tune of Rs.5000/- (Five thousand) also sought.
(iii) Additional relief to the tune of Rs.50000/- also sought for

mental harassment. (iv) Additional relief sought for the

expenditure incurred by him for purchase of new handset to

the tune of Rs.3500/- (Three thousand five hundred).
3. Per contra version filed on behalf of opposite party

No.1 pleaded therein that complaint filed by the complainant

is not maintainable. It is pleaded that complaint filed by

complainant is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties. It is

further pleaded that present complaint filed by complainant

just to harass opposite party in an illegal manner. It is

pleaded that manufacturing company is liable for

manufacturing defect. It is further pleaded that complainant

is not legally entitled for replacement of Black Berry Curve

8520 handset. It is pleaded that opposite parties No.1 & 2

are not under legal obligations to replace the Black Berry

handset to complainant as per warranty condition. Prayer for

dismissal of complaint sought.
4. Opposite party No.3 Redington India Ltd. also

filed separate version pleaded therein that opposite party No.3

Redington India Ltd. is the authorized service provider which

provides first level repair service to Black Berry customers

during warranty period as per terms and conditions imposed

by the manufacturers without receiving any consideration
3
Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)

from the customers of Black berry as per contractual

agreement between Black berry and Redington. It is further

pleaded that opposite party did not give assurances towards

the replacement of handset during warranty period. It is

pleaded that handset was exposed to liquid particles which

resulted manufacturer warranty void. Prayer of dismissal of

complaint sought. Opposite party No.2 did not file any

version despite several opportunities granted by learned

District Forum. On dated 25.03.2014 learned District Forum

struck of defence of opposite party No.2.
5. Learned District Forum partly allowed the

complaint and directed opposite parties No.1 & 3 jointly &

severally to refund Rs.9700/- (Nine thousand seven hundred)

cost of mobile phone to complainant alongwith interest at the

rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of complaint till

payment of amount. Learned District Forum in addition

further directed that complainant would be entitled for

damage for harassment to the tune of Rs.1000/-. Learned

District Forum further directed that complainant would be

entitled for litigation costs from opposite parties No.1 & 3 to

the tune of Rs.500/- (Five hundred). Learned District Forum

further directed that amount shall be paid by opposite parties

No.1 & 3 subject to condition that complainant would deposit

the defective mobile phone with opposite party No.1 within

thirty days against receipt. Feeling aggrieved against order
4
Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)

passed by Learned District Forum Shri Sarabjeet Singh

complainant filed the present appeal before State

Commission.
6. We have heard learned advocates appearing on

behalf of parties and we have also perused entire record

carefully.
7. Following points arises for determination in

present appeal.
1. Whether appeal filed by appellant is liable to be
 accepted as mentioned in memorandum of
 grounds of appeal.
2. Final order.
Findings upon point No.1 with reasons:
8. Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of

complainant on dated 25.03.2014 and 02.11.2015 has given

statement before learned District Forum that complaint

already filed by complainant be read in evidence. Learned

Advocate appearing on behalf of complainant closed the

evidence on behalf of complainant. Similarly learned

Advocate appearing on behalf of opposite party No.1 has given

statement on 22.12.2015 to the effect that version filed by

opposite party be read in evidence. Similarly learned

Advocate appearing on behalf of opposite parties No.2 & 3 has

given statement before learned District Forum on dated

22.12.2015 that version already filed be read in evidence on

behalf of opposite parties No.2 & 3.
5
Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)
9. It is held that original complaint cannot be treated

as evidence under
Consumer Protection Act
1986 because

original complaint falls within the definition of pleading and

does not fall within the definition of evidence. It is also held

that original version filed by opposite party No.3 is also

pleading and does not fall within definition of evidence as

mentioned under
Consumer Protection Act
1986. We have

carefully perused the contents of complaint and contents of

version filed by the opposite parties. Facts alleged in the

complaint by the complainant are disputed by the opposite

parties in version. It is held that when there are material

dispute inter se the parties qua facts then parties are under

legal obligation to adduce independent evidence as mentioned

under
section 13(4)
of Consumer Protection Act 1986. It is

well settled law that as per
section 13(4)
of Consumer

Protection Act 1986 parties can adduce evidence by way of

examining the witness on oath or by way of filing evidence by

way of affidavits.
10. There is recital in Annexure-C1 retail invoice bill

placed on record that Walia Electronics Shimla is only a sale

point and service would be provided by manufacturer's

authorised center. There is further condition in retail invoice

bill that goods once sold will not be taken back or replaced.

There is further recital in bill Annexure-C1 that consumer

had received good mentioned in bill to his entire satisfaction.
6
Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)
11. State Commission is of the opinion that terms &

conditions of the retail invoice bill is biding upon the parties.

It is held that parties cannot be allowed to flout the terms &

conditions of retail invoice bill Annexure-C1 placed on record.
12. We have also perused the version filed by opposite

party No.3 i.e. Redington India Ltd. placed on record.

Opposite party No.3 Redington company has admitted in the

version that opposite party No.3 i.e. Redington company has

contract with black berry company to provide repair service to

black berry customers during the warranty period as per

terms and conditions imposed by the manufacturer without

receiving any consideration from customers of black berry

company. It is proved on record that defect occurred in

handset purchased by complainant during warranty period.
13. It is well settled law that during the warranty

period company is under legal obligation to remove the defect.

Opposite party No.3 has admitted in para No.6 of version that

opposite party No.3 requested the complainant to collect

handset from the service center but complainant refused to

collect the handset. Opposite party No.3 has admitted that

mobile set was not collected by complainant. It is well settled

law that facts admitted in version need not to be proved by

the complainant. Direction of learned District Forum that

complainant would deposit the defective phone with the

opposite party within thirty days against receipt is contrary to
7
Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)

proved facts and is contrary to facts admitted by opposite

party No.3 in version. It is held that during warranty period

opposite parties No.2 & 3 are under legal obligation to repair

the mobile set.
14. It is held that in guarantee replacement of good is

permissible. It is held that in warranty the original

replacement of good is not permissible and only repair is

permissible. In view of the fact that in the present case no

guarantee was given by Black berry company Ltd. and in view

of the fact that only warranty was given and in view of fact

that Redington India Ltd. is under contractual agreement to

provide service to the customers of Black berry company free

of costs it is held that opposite party No.3 was under legal

obligation to repair handset during warranty period. Opposite

party did not produce any delivery receipt of handset signed

by complainant.
15. Plea of opposite party No.3 that handset could not

be repaired during warranty period due to exposure of

handset to liquid particles is rejected being devoid of any force

for reasons hereinafter mentioned. Opposite parties did not

file affidavit of expert in the present case in order to prove

that handset in question was exposed to liquid particles. It is

held that opposite party was under legal obligation to produce

positive evidence on record to prove that handset was exposed

to liquid particles. Plea of opposite parties that handset was
8
Sarabjeet Singh Versus Walia Electronics & Ors. (F.A. No.247/2016)

exposed to liquid particles is defeated on the concept of ipse

dixit (An assertion made without proof). In view of above

stated facts point No.1 is decided accordingly.

Point No.2: Final Order
16. In view of findings upon point No.1 above appeal is

allowed. Direction of learned District Forum to the

complainant to deposit the defective mobile phone with

opposite party No.1 within thirty days from the date of receipt

of order is set aside. Order of learned District Forum is

modified to this extent only. Retail invoice bill Annexure-C1

will form part and parcel of order. Parties are left to bear

their own costs before State Commission. File of learned

District Forum alongwith certified copy of order be sent back

forthwith and file of State Commission be consigned to record

room after due completion forthwith. Certified copy of order

be transmitted to parties forthwith free of costs strictly as per

rules. Appeal is disposed of. Pending application(s) if any

also disposed of.
Justice P.S. Rana (R)

 Vijay Pal Khachi
